decisions.reason: The GK 2.0 printer is a core, heavily invested next-generation platform that the firm promoted on its home page, so dropping it would write off major development costs and contradict its announced direction.

The Numbering module was publicly launched in two languages as part of the firm's software portfolio for variable-data printing, which ties it to the serialization strategy and makes it cheap to maintain.
The coder for non-absorbent surfaces builds on the firm's ink expertise and covers a real application niche, though its modest visibility leaves some risk of it being folded into newer models.
The CodeScan app had a page of its own and supports the traceability direction, but it cost little to develop and is peripheral, so it could be dropped without much justification if usage is low.
Inline code verification is central to the firm's announced end-to-end traceability and serialization strategy, so management will persist with it.
The layout design software was featured on the home page and supports common operation across all of the firm's systems, which makes it a visible commitment that is costly to reverse.
